canonical_statement: Provisional scope: for an integrable identically distributed sequence of pairwise independent random variables, the empirical averages converge almost surely to the expectation of the reference variable.
domain_and_universes: Provisional: Ω : Type u with MeasurableSpace; E : Type v with complete real normed additive group, measurable structure, and BorelSpace; μ : Measure Ω; X : Nat -> Ω -> E
ordered_binders: Ω : Type u and its measurable-space instance
E : Type v and its normed additive group, real normed-space, completeness, measurable-space, and Borel instances
hypotheses: Pairwise ((fun Y Z => IndepFun Y Z μ) on X)
for every i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ
conclusion: For μ-almost every ω, n |-> (n : Real)^(-1) • sum i in range n, X i ω tends to integral (X 0) dμ as n tends to infinity.
boundary_cases: The n = 0 empirical average is defined using 0^(-1) and the empty sum and does not alter the atTop limit. Degenerate measures and almost-everywhere-zero variables are not excluded at intake. Whether the historical Borel target instead requires Bernoulli trials is unresolved.
